title: Your First Django Project
description: Generate a new Django project and understand the generated files.

slides.title: Project vs. App 🧱
slides.content:
# Django Project

A **project** is the entire website – configuration, settings, and global files. An **app** is a module that does one thing (e.g., a blog, a poll, a shop).

> A project can contain many apps. Apps can be reused across projects.

We’ll create a project first.

slides.title: What Was Created? 📁
slides.content:
After running the command, you’ll see a folder `myfirstproject/` containing:

```
myfirstproject/
    manage.py
    myfirstproject/
        __init__.py
        settings.py
        urls.py
        asgi.py
        wsgi.py
```

- **`manage.py`** – A command‑line utility for interacting with your project.
- **`settings.py`** – All project configurations (database, apps, security).
- **`urls.py`** – The URL declaration for your project.
- **`wsgi.py`** / **`asgi.py`** – Entry points for web servers.

quizData.question: Which file is used to run development server and execute Django commands?
quizData.explanation: `manage.py` is the central utility – you use it to run the server, create apps, migrate databases, etc.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Keep your project folder tidy

Always name your project something descriptive. You can change the folder name later, but it’s easier to start right.
